Hook: The mistake that cost me a month, and the check that stops it now.
Main point: One mistake, what it cost, the one check that prevents it.
Call to action: Ask readers what they check before they start.
Notes: Tell it in first person, keep it short.

Hook: My weekly planning routine in six steps.
Main point: Show the routine step by step, one step per slide.
Call to action: Ask readers to share one step they would add.
Notes: Needs a cover slide with the result up front.

Hook: Which do you do first on Monday: email or planning?
Main point: Open a conversation with a simple either/or question.
Call to action: Ask readers to explain their pick in the comments.
Notes: Add a first comment with my own answer.

Hook: A client came to me with a problem I had not seen before.
Main point: What the problem was, what we tried, what worked.
Call to action: Invite readers who face the same problem to comment.
Notes: Remove the client's name and details.

Hook: Five things I would tell my first-year self.
Main point: One lesson per slide, each with a short example.
Call to action: Ask readers what they would tell their first-year self.
Notes: Reuse a past post that did well if it fits.

Hook: The checklist I run before I send any proposal.
Main point: One picture of the checklist, easy to save.
Call to action: Ask readers to save it for their next proposal.

Hook: Here is a piece of common advice in my field that I disagree with.
Main point: State the advice, say why it fails, give what I do instead.
Call to action: Ask readers whether they agree or disagree.
Notes: Be fair to the other side.

Hook: How one project went from messy to done in four steps.
Main point: Before, the steps taken, the result, what I would repeat.
Call to action: Point readers to my profile if they want to talk.
Notes: Use real numbers only if the client agrees.

Hook: How do you keep track of your tasks: paper, app or head?
Main point: A light question about tools, easy to answer.
Call to action: Ask readers to name the app or method they use.

Hook: What I learned from looking back at the last three months.
Main point: Two things that worked, one that did not, one change.
Call to action: Ask readers what they changed this quarter.
Notes: Look at past posts for ideas first.

Hook: Three questions to ask before you take on a new project.
Main point: One question per slide, with why it matters.
Call to action: Ask readers which question they would add.
Notes: Link to an earlier post on the same topic.

Hook: A kind note from a client, with their permission.
Main point: One quote on a plain background.
Call to action: Thank them and invite readers to get in touch.
